## Story-level uncertainties

- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later works give the man a name and say who he was; the text itself only calls him a man from the farthest part of the city.
- Hadith to add later: reports about the man who warned Musa, with a named grader for each; none is used here.

## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. The man who came running  (`#the-man-who-came-running`)

Cited ayat: 28:20-21

> **28:20** وَجَآءَ رَجُلٌ مِّنْ أَقْصَا ٱلْمَدِينَةِ يَسْعَىٰ قَالَ يَٰمُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّ ٱلْمَلَأَ يَأْتَمِرُونَ بِكَ لِيَقْتُلُوكَ فَٱخْرُجْ إِنِّى لَكَ مِنَ ٱلنَّٰصِحِينَ
>
> **28:21** فَخَرَجَ مِنْهَا خَآئِفًا يَتَرَقَّبُ قَالَ رَبِّ نَجِّنِى مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

### Claims

**c1** (28:20): A man came running from the farthest part of the city and said to Musa that the chiefs were plotting against him to kill him, so he should leave, since he was one of those who advised him well.

**c2** (28:21): Musa left the city fearful and watchful, and said, my Lord, save me from the wrongdoing people.

### One-minute summary

A man came running from the farthest part of the city and warned Musa that the chiefs were plotting to kill him [c1]. Musa left the city fearful and asked his Lord to save him from the wrongdoing people [c2].

### Complete story

A man came running from the farthest part of the city and said to Musa that the chiefs were plotting against him to kill him, so he should leave, since he was one of those who advised him well [c1]. Musa left the city fearful and watchful, and said, my Lord, save me from the wrongdoing people [c2].

### Deep study

The ayah gives the man's words as advice from one who wishes him well [c1]. It does not say how he knew of the plot [c1].

### Kids mode

A man ran from the far side of the city to warn Musa [c1]. Musa left the city and asked his Lord to save him [c2].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that a warning was given and heeded [c1][c2]. Another is that Musa, after leaving, turned to his Lord [c2].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: the man's name, his faith or his relation to Musa.
- Not established: the name of the city, or who the chiefs were.
- Not established: how the man knew of the plot, or what became of him.
